audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Is post-recovery KZG commitment verification performed for ALL recovered cells and proofs?
audit_items.state_context: data_columns_reconstruct.go: reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars calls peerdas.ReconstructDataColumnSidecars then immediately saves+schedules broadcast with NO intermediate commitment verification. data_column_sidecars.go mergeAvailableSidecars also calls peerdas.ReconstructDataColumnSidecars and uses results directly. ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs takes only cellIndices+cells, does NOT accept commitments, cannot verify against block commitments.

phase1.summary: VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED: ReconstructDataColumnSidecars calls kzg.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs (erasure coding recovery) and then directly promotes results to VerifiedRODataColumn via blocks.NewVerifiedRODataColumn WITHOUT calling VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs. The C library ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs does not accept commitments as input — it cannot verify recovered cells against block commitments. The comment at lines 108-109 claiming 'reconstructed sidecars are also verified' is a false logical inference.
state_anomalies: Trust escalation without verification: NewVerifiedRODataColumn called at reconstruction.go:117 from beacon-chain/core/peerdas package, violating the contract that this method 'should only be used by the verification package'
Recovery function RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs takes only cellIndices+partialCells; no commitment parameter; cannot cryptographically verify recovered cells against block commitments
Post-reconstruction: no call to VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs before VerifiedRODataColumn promotion
Reconstructed VerifiedRODataColumn objects saved to dataColumnStorage and scheduled for broadcast without any additional verification gate

phase2.summary: Symbolic execution confirms the missing verification path. After wg.Wait() at reconstruction.go:99, cellsAndProofs contains erasure-recovered cells and proofs. The proofs are computed by ckzg4844 using the trusted setup but are NOT verified against kzgCommitments from the block. The function VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs in p2p_interface.go (which calls kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch with commitment, cell_index, cell, proof) is never invoked.
phase2.attack_scenario: Storage corruption scenario (no crypto break required): A storage backend returning corrupted cell data for cells already marked as stored produces corrupted input to ReconstructDataColumnSidecars. The function performs polynomial interpolation from corrupted inputs, computes internally-consistent but commitment-mismatched proofs, promotes to VerifiedRODataColumn, saves to storage, and broadcasts to P2P network. The corruption propagates to all peers receiving the broadcast, labeled as cryptographically verified data.
phase2.timing_dependencies: broadcastMissingDataColumnsTimeIntoSlotMin (1s) + random slack (0-2s) delay before broadcast, but save-to-storage occurs immediately; no verification window in between

entry_points: P2P gossip data column sidecar subnet → sidecar stored → reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars triggered
P2P RPC sync → FetchDataColumnSidecars → mergeAvailableSidecars → ReconstructDataColumnSidecars
phase2_5.attacker_controlled: partially — attacker cannot forge KZG proofs for individual cells without breaking BLS12-381 discrete log; however storage corruption and Byzantine storage backends bypass this protection
phase2_5.classification: defense-in-depth-failure (pure P2P crypto attack) to directly-exploitable (storage corruption / Byzantine storage)

phase3.invariant_tested: If all input sidecars are VerifiedRODataColumn, then all reconstructed sidecars are correctly verified against the block's KZG commitments
phase3.justification: The claimed invariant is false. VerifiedRODataColumn status of input only guarantees each input cell was verified at reception time. It does NOT guarantee: (1) cells haven't been corrupted in storage since then, (2) erasure recovery produces commitment-consistent output (ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs does not verify against commitments), (3) all future callers will maintain input-verification invariants. The missing post-recovery call to VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs (kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch with commitment, cell_index, cell, proof) leaves an unguarded trust promotion. Package boundary contract for NewVerifiedRODataColumn is violated.
additional_issues: blobSidecarsFromDataColumnSidecars in same file calls NewVerifiedROBlob without post-reconstruction blob KZG proof verification
mergeAvailableSidecars in data_column_sidecars.go has identical missing-verification pattern

phase3_5.recommendation: After wg.Wait() in ReconstructDataColumnSidecars, after assembling reconstructedSidecars via dataColumnsSidecars, convert to RODataColumn slice and call peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs before promoting to VerifiedRODataColumn. This adds a cryptographic gate ensuring recovered cells match block commitments.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Do ALL callers of recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs verify recovered data against original commitment?
audit_items.state_context: All callers of ReconstructDataColumnSidecars identified: (1) data_columns_reconstruct.go:71 in reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars, (2) data_column_sidecars.go:522 in mergeAvailableSidecars, (3) reconstruction.go:245 in ReconstructBlobs (calls self). None of these callers call VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs after receiving reconstructed output.

phase1.summary: VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED: Caller audit of kzg.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs (called only through ReconstructDataColumnSidecars) reveals NO caller performs post-recovery KZG commitment verification. The two primary production callers — reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars (broadcast path) and mergeAvailableSidecars (fetch path) — both consume VerifiedRODataColumn results from ReconstructDataColumnSidecars without any additional commitment verification. The verification function VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs exists but is never invoked post-reconstruction.
state_anomalies: reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars: saves reconstructed sidecars to storage and schedules broadcast — no VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs call
mergeAvailableSidecars: passes reconstructed sidecars back to callers for consensus/sync use — no VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs call
ReconstructBlobs (reconstruction.go:245): uses reconstructed VerifiedRODataColumn for blob reconstruction — no commitment verification
The VerifiedRODataColumn label is propagated across all callers as if it represents post-reconstruction cryptographic verification

phase2.summary: All 3 production callers of ReconstructDataColumnSidecars are confirmed to not call VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs on results. This is a systemic caller responsibility violation — the verification is documented as the caller's responsibility in the property (PROP-W5B14-17) but no caller performs it. The reconstruction.go comment actively misleads callers into believing no post-verification is needed.
phase2.attack_scenario: Any scenario where input cells to ReconstructDataColumnSidecars are corrupted produces undetected propagation of invalid data. With reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars: corrupted storage → ReconstructDataColumnSidecars → save to storage → broadcast to network (after 1-3s delay). With mergeAvailableSidecars: peer provides corrupted cells that each individually pass VerifyCellKZGProofBatch → reconstruction from corrupted inputs → returned as VerifiedRODataColumn to sync consumers.
phase2.timing_dependencies: No timing dependency for the core vulnerability — missing verification is a static code defect

phase3.invariant_tested: All callers of recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs verify recovered data against original commitment before use
phase3.justification: Exhaustive search of codebase via mcp__tree_sitter__find_text for 'ReconstructDataColumnSidecars' identified 3 production callers. None invoke VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs on the output. The verification function peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs that calls kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch(commitment, index, cell, proof) is only called during incoming P2P validation (before storing to DB), not after reconstruction.

phase3_5.recommendation: Add VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs call either (a) inside ReconstructDataColumnSidecars before returning, or (b) in all callers immediately after receiving reconstructed results. Option (a) is preferred as it enforces the contract at the function boundary.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Can a malicious P2P peer cause a validator to distribute corrupted recovered cells?
audit_items.state_context: reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars acquires reconstructionLock for reconstruction phase but releases it before broadcast. broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars loads from storage and broadcasts. The reconstructionLock prevents concurrent reconstructions but does not add a verification checkpoint.

phase1.summary: VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED WITH NUANCE: A pure P2P cryptographic attack requires forging KZG proofs (infeasible). However, the attack surface is broader — any corruption between initial P2P verification and use in reconstruction enables propagation of corrupted cells. Specifically: (1) A Byzantine peer providing exactly MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct() = 64 cells where each cell passes individual KZG proof verification BUT the combination is engineered for equivocation, (2) Storage corruption between initial storage and reconstruction retrieval, (3) Memory corruption. The broadcast path (reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars) DOES save and broadcast reconstructed data without post-reconstruction verification.
state_anomalies: Cells loaded from dataColumnStorage.Get(root, nil) at reconstruction.go:65 are trusted as-is — no re-verification before input to ReconstructDataColumnSidecars
After reconstruction, no VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs call before save to storage
After save, broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars broadcasts from storage — again no verification
The reconstructionLock only prevents concurrent reconstruction, does not verify output

phase2.summary: The most concrete exploit path: (1) A malicious storage backend (e.g., a corrupted disk sector or memory fault) alters stored cell data. (2) reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars retrieves corrupted cells, calls ReconstructDataColumnSidecars. (3) Reconstruction produces cells that are mathematically inconsistent with the block's KZG commitments. (4) These are saved as VerifiedRODataColumn and broadcast to peers as legitimate data. (5) Peers accepting this data (which may pass their individual receipt verification if they don't reconstruct again) store corrupted data. For the pure P2P Byzantine scenario: a single peer cannot forge KZG proofs; but if an attacker can make exactly MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct()-1 valid columns available AND provide the remaining 1 column as corrupted data that somehow passes VerifyCellKZGProofBatch (which it cannot without crypto break), reconstruction is triggered on corrupted input.
phase2.attack_scenario: Storage fault injection: Corrupt one cell in dataColumnStorage for a slot. When reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars triggers, it reads the corrupted cell among its inputs, performs Reed-Solomon recovery using the corrupted cell as a basis point, produces a polynomial that does not match original commitments, computes KZG proofs for the wrong polynomial, wraps in VerifiedRODataColumn, saves to storage, broadcasts to peers. Peers receive 'verified' data that is cryptographically inconsistent with the block commitments.
phase2.timing_dependencies: Reconstruction triggered automatically when storedColumnsCount >= MinimumColumnCountToReconstruct() and < numberOfColumns — attacker window is the interval between a valid cell count threshold being reached and full reconstruction

entry_points: P2P gossip → triggers reconstruction when threshold reached
phase2_5.attacker_controlled: partially (storage corruption required for most concrete scenarios; pure P2P attack requires KZG break)

phase3.invariant_tested: A malicious P2P peer cannot cause distribution of corrupted recovered cells
phase3.justification: While a direct P2P attacker cannot forge individual cell KZG proofs (requires discrete log break on BLS12-381), the SYSTEM invariant fails because: (1) the code does not enforce post-reconstruction verification, creating a fragile defense-in-depth; (2) any indirect attack that corrupts stored cells (storage fault, memory error, Byzantine storage implementation) bypasses the P2P verification layer; (3) the broadcast path has no additional verification gate. The security of the broadcast path depends entirely on the correctness of the storage layer, which is not cryptographically guaranteed.

phase3_5.notes: The pure P2P exploit requires a crypto break (low risk), but the broader system vulnerability (storage corruption propagation, defense-in-depth failure) is confirmed. Bug bounty eligibility depends on scope — if storage fault scenarios are in scope, this is directly exploitable.
phase3_5.recommendation: Add VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs call on reconstructed sidecars before broadcasting. This is a single-function-call fix that eliminates the entire class of post-reconstruction propagation vulnerabilities.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does the validator node trust reconstructed data without cryptographic verification?
audit_items.state_context: Data flow after reconstruction: VerifiedRODataColumn → dataColumnStorage.Save → dataColumnStorage.Get (by other code paths) → consensus/sync use. The VerifiedRODataColumn type is used by consensus-critical code as an indicator of cryptographic validity. Implicit trust assumption: VerifiedRODataColumn = safe to use without re-checking.

phase1.summary: VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED: The validator node DOES trust reconstructed data without cryptographic verification. The specific implicit trust assumption is: 'VerifiedRODataColumn from ReconstructDataColumnSidecars is cryptographically verified against block commitments.' This assumption is FALSE. The VerifiedRODataColumn type carries semantic weight in the Prysm codebase (used by consensus-critical consumers) but reconstruction.go escalates unverified data to this type. The kzgCommitments used to build reconstructed sidecar structures come from the reference input sidecar (line 67: referenceSidecar.KzgCommitments) but are never used to VERIFY the recovered cells — they are only structurally embedded in the output.
state_anomalies: kzgCommitments from line 67 used structurally (embedded in reconstructed sidecar) but never used to verify recovered cells via VerifyCellKZGProofBatch
VerifiedRODataColumn used by dataColumnStorage.Save without re-verification at retrieval time

ReconstructBlobs (reconstruction.go:206-249) calls ReconstructDataColumnSidecars and then uses results to reconstruct blobs — again no commitment verification on the reconstructed column sidecars before blob extraction
blobSidecarsFromDataColumnSidecars calls NewVerifiedROBlob after blob reconstruction from recovered cells — no BlobKZGProofVerification

phase2.summary: The implicit trust assumption is exploitable via: (1) ReconstructBlobs path — blob reconstruction using unverified reconstructed columns could produce invalid blobs labeled as VerifiedROBlob; (2) Any code that receives VerifiedRODataColumn from the reconstruction subsystem and skips re-verification because of the type guarantee. The type system is being misused to propagate a false verification claim.
phase2.attack_scenario: ReconstructBlobs flow: Client requests blobs → FetchDataColumnSidecars → mergeAvailableSidecars triggers ReconstructDataColumnSidecars → reconstructed (unverified) VerifiedRODataColumn passed to blobSidecarsFromDataColumnSidecars → VerifiedROBlob objects returned to client without post-reconstruction blob KZG proof verification. If underlying cells are corrupted, client receives corrupted VerifiedROBlob objects.
phase2.timing_dependencies: No timing dependency — static vulnerability in data flow

entry_points: Block sync blob retrieval → ReconstructBlobs → ReconstructDataColumnSidecars

phase3.invariant_tested: Validator node verifies reconstructed data cryptographically before using it for any consensus-critical operation
phase3.justification: The kzgCommitments present in the reconstructed sidecar structure are never used to call VerifyCellKZGProofBatch on the recovered cells. The 'proof' fields in the CellsAndProofs returned by RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs are KZG proofs computed by the ckzg4844 library for the recovered polynomial — they are NOT verified against the block commitments within the library. VerifyCellKZGProofBatch(commitment, index, cell, proof) would detect any mismatch, but this function is never called post-reconstruction. The ReconstructBlobs path compounding: unverified VerifiedRODataColumn → blobSidecarsFromDataColumnSidecars → unverified VerifiedROBlob.

phase3_5.recommendation: In ReconstructDataColumnSidecars, after dataColumnsSidecars returns, convert reconstructed sidecars to []blocks.RODataColumn and call peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs before wrapping in VerifiedRODataColumn. This ensures kzgCommitments are used to VERIFY (not just structurally embed) the recovered cells.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is the 'original_commitment' used for verification sourced from trusted consensus, not recovered data?
audit_items.state_context: KZG commitments for reconstruction come from referenceSidecar.KzgCommitments (the first input VerifiedRODataColumn). These commitments ARE derived from the block header and verified via KzgCommitmentsInclusionProof during initial P2P validation. However, they are NOT fetched from the local beacon state/finalized block header during reconstruction — they come from the input sidecars. If input sidecars could be tampered with after initial verification, commitment source integrity is broken.

phase1.summary: PARTIALLY MITIGATED with RESIDUAL CONCERN: The KZG commitments used in reconstruction come from input VerifiedRODataColumn sidecars, which had their KzgCommitmentsInclusionProof verified against the block header's body root during P2P receipt (via VerifyDataColumnSidecarInclusionProof in p2p_interface.go). This provides a cryptographic chain from the commitments to the signed block header. HOWEVER: (1) these commitments are STRUCTURALLY embedded in reconstructed sidecars but NOT USED to verify recovered cells, so the commitment source integrity is moot if verification is never performed; (2) the commitment source does not guard against storage corruption between receipt and reconstruction use.
state_anomalies: KzgCommitments from referenceSidecar (input sidecar, P2P-verified) embedded in reconstructed sidecars but never used to call VerifyCellKZGProofBatch on recovered cells
Commitment source integrity is preserved for the P2P path but meaningless if the verification step is missing
Storage corruption between initial storage and reconstruction retrieval can corrupt both cells AND commitments

phase2.summary: The commitment source question is secondary to the missing verification. Even with trusted commitments, the vulnerability exists because the commitments are NEVER USED to verify the recovered cells (VerifyCellKZGProofBatch is never called post-reconstruction). The commitment source being trusted (from P2P-verified sidecars, not from recovered data) is actually correct and not itself a vulnerability — but the ABSENCE of using those commitments for verification is the bug.
phase2.notes: For CHK-0145 specifically: the commitment IS sourced from trusted input (P2P-verified VerifiedRODataColumn), NOT from the recovered/reconstructed data itself. This specific sub-check passes. The block header → body root → KzgCommitmentsInclusionProof chain is maintained. However, this does not mitigate the parent vulnerability (CHK-0141/0142) because the correct commitments exist but are unused for verification.
phase2.timing_dependencies: TOCTOU not applicable for commitment source — commitment is determined at function call, not time-of-use

entry_points: P2P gossip validation → commitment verified via inclusion proof → stored in VerifiedRODataColumn → used as reference sidecar in reconstruction
phase2_5.attacker_controlled: limited — attacker cannot substitute commitments from recovered data; commitments are block-anchored

phase3.invariant_tested: The original_commitment used for verification is sourced from trusted consensus, not recovered data
phase3.justification: The invariant for CHK-0145's specific question IS satisfied: kzgCommitments at reconstruction.go:68 come from referenceSidecar.KzgCommitments, which was P2P-verified (KzgCommitmentsInclusionProof verified against SignedBlockHeader body root). Commitments are NOT derived from or influenced by the recovered cell data. HOWEVER, the guard is insufficient because these correctly-sourced commitments are never actually used to verify the recovered cells — they are embedded in the output structure but VerifyCellKZGProofBatch is never called. The 'correct source' property is necessary but not sufficient — the commitments must also be USED for verification.
additional_issues: If an attacker could corrupt the stored KzgCommitments field (storage corruption), the commitments would be wrong — but this is the same storage corruption scenario as CHK-0143
The primary vulnerability (CHK-0141) renders CHK-0145's guarantee meaningless — correctly-sourced commitments that are never used for verification provide no security benefit

phase3_5.notes: CHK-0145's specific sub-question (commitment source integrity) is answered: commitments ARE from trusted consensus, NOT from recovered data. This specific property is correctly implemented. However, the vulnerability is confirmed at the system level because these correctly-sourced commitments are never used to verify recovered cells. Bug bounty eligibility derives from the parent property (PROP-W5B14-17) being violated: post-recovery verification is missing regardless of commitment source correctness.
phase3_5.recommendation: Add VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs call after reconstruction in ReconstructDataColumnSidecars. The correctly-sourced kzgCommitments (already present in input sidecars) should be passed to VerifyCellKZGProofBatch via this call. This will complete the security chain: correct commitment source + verification of recovered cells against those commitments.
